clue.text: Awfully spare: chaps refuse to be seen here

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for places where rubbish lies

indicators.note: done awfully means done badly, so the letters come out in a botched, jumbled order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Some men flatly decline to show their faces anywhere near this place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'refuse' looks like a verb meaning decline, but it is the noun: rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaps of discarded junk are exactly where waste and rubbish would be visible lying around.

clue.text: Audibly rise, being angry

indicators.note: something heard rather than read is judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: to soar is to rise high

explanation.surface: Someone's voice climbs as their temper flares.
explanation.walkthrough: SOAR and SORE are pronounced the same in most accents.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling sore is an informal, chiefly American way of being upset or resentful with someone.

clue.text: Premier, a Republican, going up slope

indicators.note: in a down clue, travelling upward means reading from the bottom back to the top

blocks.note: PM is short for Prime Minister, the premier
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: A prime minister and a Republican ally see their fortunes climbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' paints a rising career, but in a down answer it flips the letters upward.
explanation.definitionFit: An inclined surface joining two levels, used by wheelchairs or vehicles, is a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Early parts of play: rôles include Victor, Amanda; they encounter – lucklessly, in vacation – Elyot, Sibyl!

definitions.text: Early parts of play: rôles include Victor, Amanda; they encounter – lucklessly, in vacation – Elyot, Sibyl!

indicators.note: the earliest part of each word is its opening letter, so only those are kept

blocks.clueFragment: play: rôles include Victor, Amanda; they encounter – lucklessly, in vacation – Elyot, Sibyl
blocks.note: the opening letters of the twelve words in order

explanation.surface: A plot summary: four characters meet by bad luck while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Noël Coward's 1930 comedy has divorced Elyot and Amanda honeymooning with new spouses Sibyl and Victor in adjoining hotel rooms; the whole clue is its synopsis as well as the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue summarises the plot of Coward's famous comedy, naming its four principal characters and their unlucky holiday meeting.

clue.text: Part of weekend I've spent finding salad

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun for salad leaves

indicators.note: a part is a portion of something larger, here a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Someone spent part of their weekend shopping for salad.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer straddles the end of 'weekend', all of 'I've' and the first letter of 'spent'.
explanation.definitionFit: Endive is a bitter leafy vegetable commonly eaten raw in mixed salads, related to chicory.

clue.text: I ran into quiet hall, not half finding ferocious type

indicators.note: running into something means entering it, so one piece goes inside another
having only half of something means the other half is dropped

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
taken as written
the first half of the four-letter word

explanation.surface: Someone dashed into a hushed hall and met a fearsome character.
explanation.walkthrough: P wraps the run of letters from 'I ran', then the first two letters of 'hall' follow.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American freshwater fish is notorious for sharp teeth and savage feeding frenzies, a byword for ferocity.

clue.text: Ring friend, wanting gemstone

blocks.note: the letter O is ring-shaped
a pal is a friend

explanation.surface: A friend phones, hoping for a precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' suggests a phone call or jewellery; here it is just the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: This milky, iridescent mineral is valued as a precious stone in jewellery.

clue.text: Master craving act of delaying

blocks.note: a pro, or professional, is a master of a skill
a longing is a craving

explanation.surface: An expert yearns to put things off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a noun phrase, and the answer works as a verbal noun: the prolonging of talks.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawing something out so it lasts longer amounts to stalling its end, a gerund used as a noun.

clue.text: Support Scotswoman to run: first minister?

blocks.note: a leg supports a table or a body
Isla is a popular Scottish girl's name
taken as written
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Backing a Scottish woman's bid to become First Minister of Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a first minister is only one example of a lawmaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A head of government such as Scotland's First Minister is an elected parliamentarian who makes laws, so one example of the type.

clue.text: Sells cheaply what you may be left with after division

definitions.text: what you may be left with after division

blocks.note: first meaning: a publisher disposes of unsold stock of books at a reduced price

blocks.clueFragment: what you may be left with after division
blocks.note: second meaning: the amount over when one number does not divide another exactly

explanation.surface: A shop flogging leftover goods cheaply after a split.
explanation.walkthrough: One sense is a verb from the book trade, the other the arithmetic noun.
explanation.definitionFit: In publishing the verb means discount surplus copies, while in arithmetic the noun is the leftover amount from dividing.

clue.text: Vietnamese money's sound as a bell

blocks.note: first meaning: the currency of Vietnam
second meaning: the deep ringing noise a bell makes

explanation.surface: Vietnam's currency is in perfectly healthy shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' is an idiom for in perfect condition; here it simply means the noise of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Vietnam's monetary unit has this name, and it is also the imitative word for a deep chime.

clue.text: Blunt implements brandished, I subvert Kent

indicators.note: a brandished weapon is waved wildly about, so the letters are thrown around too

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel waves blunt weapons while undermining an English county.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; here it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: These table utensils have rounded edges for spreading, so they are deliberately dull rather than sharp tools.

clue.text: Daredevil aunt drove us crazy

indicators.note: something crazy is disordered and wild, so the letters lose their order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A reckless aunt's driving terrifies the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daredevil' reads as a noun in the surface but works as an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A daredevil attitude is bold and risk-taking, keen on thrills, which is what the adjective describes.

clue.text: Everyman, say: somebody conforming to convention (at first)

indicators.note: placing something first puts it at the front of the pair

blocks.note: proper behaviour follows accepted standards
a somebody is a big name, a famous person

explanation.surface: The setter describes themself as a conventional, respectable sort.
explanation.walkthrough: Everyman is the name of this crossword's setter and of a medieval morality play; capitalised, it is a name for one specific thing.
explanation.definitionFit: A capitalised word naming one particular person, title or place is grammatically a proper noun, and Everyman is one.

clue.text: After a time, acts of praise for properties

indicators.note: coming after something means being placed behind it in the line

blocks.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time
tributes are acts of praise or homage

explanation.surface: Eventually, some houses get the praise they deserve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'properties' suggests buildings, but it means characteristics.
explanation.definitionFit: Qualities or features belonging to something are its characteristics, a sense shared by both words.

clue.text: Del Boy and kin needing no introduction: rogues

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so having none means the first letter goes

blocks.note: Del Boy is Derek Trotter of the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses, so his family is this surname

explanation.surface: A famous TV family of wheeler-dealers is so well known it needs no introduction.
explanation.walkthrough: Only Fools and Horses is a much-loved BBC comedy about the market-trading Trotter brothers in Peckham; dropping their T leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old-fashioned British words for unscrupulous, dishonest or unpleasant people.

clue.text: Some giant iguanas somewhere in W. Indies

indicators.note: some of a thing is only a portion, here a run of consecutive letters

blocks.note: the letters span the two words

explanation.surface: Large lizards live on a Caribbean island.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer starts inside 'giant' and runs into 'iguanas'.
explanation.definitionFit: This island belongs to the Leeward group in the eastern Caribbean, so it is one location in that region.

clue.text: Fail to be seen in curly hairdo every day

indicators.note: something visible within another thing sits inside it

blocks.note: a perm is a permanent wave, a curly hairstyle
an engine that fails dies

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to be seen in curls any day of the week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fail to be seen' looks like a single phrase meaning avoid appearing, but it splits into a verb and a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin phrase means for each day, used for daily allowances or rates in English.

clue.text: Hi-tech devices, they're often dangled over cots

blocks.note: first meaning: cellphones, in British usage
second meaning: hanging decorations of balanced shapes that move in the air

explanation.surface: Gadgets parents hang above a baby's bed.
explanation.walkthrough: A cot is a baby's crib in British English; a mobile phone is a cellphone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both portable phones and hanging nursery ornaments that turn in moving air.

clue.text: City to twice enthral Ronald

indicators.note: to enthral is to hold captive, so one piece is held within another

blocks.note: the word written two times
Ron is short for Ronald

explanation.surface: A city captivates a man called Ronald again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: The pair of TOs split apart with RON between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada's largest urban centre, the capital of Ontario, is a major North American metropolis.

clue.text: Raw mayonnaise dressing

blocks.note: first meaning: served uncooked and minced
second meaning: a sauce of mayonnaise with capers and gherkins

explanation.surface: An unprocessed mayonnaise-based dressing.
explanation.walkthrough: Both meanings come from French cookery; tartare sauce is the usual British spelling of tartar sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Steak tartare is minced uncooked beef, and the sauce is mayonnaise with chopped pickles and capers.

clue.text: One proving there's honour among thieves?

definitions.text: One proving there's honour among thieves?

blocks.clueFragment: One proving there's honour among thieves?
blocks.note: surface reading: someone showing that criminals keep faith with one another
setter's reading: an honour is a title, so a titled noble who is also a plunderer

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says there is honour among thieves, meaning loyalty; read literally, honour is a noble rank held by a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: Historically a feudal lord who plundered travellers, later a ruthless tycoon; either way a nobleman who steals.

clue.text: Is the French land entirely surrounded by water?

blocks.note: taken as written
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Asking whether France is completely encircled by sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The question reads as a geography query; 'the French' supplies the masculine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A dictionary-style description of an island, for which the answer is the poetic synonym.

clue.text: Correct deadlifts at regular intervals

indicators.note: evenly spaced steps pick out every second letter and skip the rest

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: Fixing weightlifting technique in a gym session done regularly.
explanation.walkthrough: A deadlift is a weightlifting move; take every other letter starting from the second.
explanation.definitionFit: To revise text by fixing its errors is to amend it, a plain verb synonym.

clue.text: Old tenor given note? On reflection, one that sings higher

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things backwards

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
T is the abbreviation for tenor
la is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: An ageing tenor, handed a note, realises someone else has the higher part.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition stays in the musical scene: the voice above the tenor.
explanation.definitionFit: This voice part sits above the tenor in four-part harmony, so its singer takes a higher line.

clue.text: Unwise, raging lad is ... devil

indicators.note: something raging is out of control, so the letters are wildly rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A furious boy behaves like a little devil, which is foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis bridges the two halves of the fodder across the pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without good judgement or sound counsel is lacking wisdom, a straightforward adjective synonym.

clue.text: Drugs, they say for freedom from discomfort

indicators.note: what people say is spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: E is slang for an ecstasy tablet, so several are Es

explanation.surface: Users claim narcotics bring relief from pain.
explanation.walkthrough: E for ecstasy is a convention; Es said out loud matches the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Relief from pain, worry or effort is comfort and relaxation, the noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Dunces Society intended to skip a test

indicators.note: skipping something means passing over it, so a letter is left out

blocks.note: asses are fools
S is the abbreviation for society
intended means meant
the letter removed

explanation.surface: A society for slow learners plans to dodge an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The removed A is taken from the middle of MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: An exam or evaluation measuring someone's ability is an appraisal, a common noun synonym.
